topic: What a network is: hosts, links, switches
title: Two PCs and a switch
instructions:
## The smallest network

Two PCs are plugged into a switch, but neither has an address yet, so they cannot talk.

## Do this

1. Click **PC1** and give it the address `192.168.1.10` with mask `255.255.255.0`.
2. Click **PC2** and give it a different address in the same subnet, for example `192.168.1.20`, with the same mask.
3. Use the **Ping** tool to ping PC2 from PC1. Read the trace: the switch forwards the frame, PC2 answers.
4. Press **Check my network**.

A switch needs no IP address: it forwards frames by MAC address, not by IP.
hints: Both PCs must share the first three numbers (192.168.1) and have a mask of 255.255.255.0.
The last number must be different on each PC, and between 1 and 254.
In the Ping tool choose From: PC1 and type PC2 or its address, then press ping.
realityNote: On a real switch you would also see the link lights come on when the cable is plugged in, and `ipconfig` (Windows) or `ip addr` (Linux) shows the address you set. The first ping is often slow because the PC must first ask "who has 192.168.1.20?" (ARP) before it can send.
